- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or add early mean-reversion term.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and price is falling, model often underestimates further drop; add 2–3% downward adjustment or extend decay curve.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; apply 1–2% upward bias for low-sentiment periods.
- If last 3–5 days show strong sentiment reversal (e.g., from 0.67 to 0.0), model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day average or add 0.5–1.0% correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model shows steady upward trend with no sentiment support, reduce slope by 10–15% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often misreads sentiment; apply sentiment decay factor (e.g., 0.8x sentiment weight) to forecast.
